summary:
I developed an interactive 3D website, hosted through GitHub, that allows users to explore the surface of Mars in a detailed and immersive way. The website provides a 3D view of the planet, allowing users to navigate and discover different geographical locations using an integrated search bar. It includes zoom-in and zoom-out controls, as well as a home button that resets the view to its original zoom level and position.

The website also features a dedicated altitude mode, which displays the elevation of different locations across Mars using a color-coded scale ranging from low to high altitudes, clearly shown on the right side of the screen. In both exploration modes, users can view the exact geographical coordinates of the location they are examining.

The goal of this project is to make exploring Mars more interactive, accessible, and educational. By combining 3D visualization, geographical coordinates, and altitude data, the website helps users better understand the planet's surface and its diverse terrain.
details:
Project Details – Mars Explorer: Interactive 3D Exploration of the Red Planet

What does the project do and how does it work?

Mars Explorer is an interactive 3D website that allows users to explore the surface of Mars and discover its different geographical locations. Hosted through GitHub, the website provides an interactive planetary visualization that users can navigate directly from their browser. It includes a search bar to find specific locations, zoom-in and zoom-out controls to examine the planet at different scales, and a home button that resets the view to its original position and zoom level.

The website also features an altitude mode that allows users to visualize the elevation of different areas across Mars. Different colors represent different altitude levels, ranging from lower to higher elevations, with a color scale displayed on the right side of the screen. In both exploration modes, users can see the exact coordinates of the location they are viewing.

What are its benefits and intended impact?

The main benefit of Mars Explorer is that it makes exploring Mars more accessible, visual, and interactive. Instead of relying only on photographs or complicated scientific maps, users can navigate the planet themselves and gain a better understanding of its geography. The altitude visualization also helps users recognize differences in the planet's terrain and understand how elevation varies across its surface.

The intended impact is to encourage curiosity about planetary science, make information about Mars easier to explore, and provide an educational experience for students, space enthusiasts, and anyone interested in space exploration.

What tools and technologies were used?

The project was developed using TypeScript, CesiumJS, and Vite, with GitHub Pages used for hosting. CesiumJS provides the interactive 3D globe and visualization capabilities, while NASA-derived Mars geographical and elevation data supports the exploration and altitude features.

What makes the project creative and innovative?

The creative aspect of Mars Explorer is the combination of interactive 3D planetary exploration and altitude visualization in one website. Users are not simply viewing a static image of Mars; they can actively explore different locations, search for geographical areas, inspect coordinates, and switch between two different visualization modes. The color-coded altitude system makes geographical information easier to understand visually.

What factors did the team consider?

During development, I considered accessibility, ease of navigation, visual clarity, and the educational value of the website. I wanted the interface to be simple enough for beginners while still providing useful geographical information. I also considered how to make the different features work together smoothly, ensuring that users could explore the planet, locate specific areas, and understand altitude information without unnecessary complexity.

Ultimately, Mars Explorer aims to transform the exploration of Mars into an engaging and interactive experience that brings the Red Planet closer to everyone.

*NOTE:

Scientific Data and Visualization

Mars Explorer uses real Mars geographical and elevation data derived from NASA resources, including the Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA). This allows users to explore actual Martian terrain rather than a fictional or artificially generated representation.

The altitude visualization translates elevation values into a color-coded representation, making it easier to distinguish lower and higher regions across the planet. Users can also inspect the geographical coordinates of the locations they explore.

A future development goal is to introduce a 2D interactive Mars map, similar to Google Maps, allowing users to navigate the planet through a flat geographical interface in addition to the existing 3D experience. This feature is planned for a future version and is not yet implemented.
